micro.breaks Spec
Last updated 3 October 2026 · V1 test week

micro.breaks

Move a little, every hour you sit.

Problem

Office workers spend most of the workday seated, in long unbroken blocks. An objective study of 231 office workers found they sat for 79% of work hours, and 42% of work hours in bouts of 30 min or more. Nothing in the workday cues them to stop. By the time they notice, the cost has landed: a stiff neck or lower back, an afternoon energy crash, focus that fades before the work is done. Low back pain is the single leading cause of disability worldwide, affecting 619 million people in 2020.

The fix is small and proven. Five minutes of walking every 30 min cut blood-sugar spikes by 58%, lowered blood pressure by 4–5 mmHg, and reduced fatigue compared with sitting all day. Yet existing break reminders don't stick: they fire mid-call or mid-flow, get snoozed, then switched off. When people do stop, they don't know what to do with two minutes, especially in an open space. And nothing shows whether they are actually moving more.

79%

of work hours spent sitting by office workers

42%

of work hours in sitting bouts of 30 min or more

−58%

blood-sugar spikes with 5 min of walking every 30 min

Who it's for

  • Desk-bound office workers on a laptop 6–8 h a day, mostly in Chrome, working from home and from an open-space office.
  • V1 user: the author. One test week, one person, to prove the habit forms before anyone else uses it.
  • They know they should move and still don't, the way people snooze an alarm. A reminder is not enough; they need friction.

Benchmark

  • Wayk: an alarm you can only silence by completing a mission. Same idea here: the break prompt only goes away when you move.
  • Pushscroll: a physical action is the price of a bad habit (scrolling). Ours: moving is the price of staying at your desk.

Goal

Success after the test week.

  • ≤ 60 minLongest seated streak, every working day.
  • ≥ 80%of break prompts end in a completed mission, not a skip.
  • YesAt the end of the week, I want to keep using it.

Solution

A Chrome extension. A battery on every new tab drains while you sit. When it is empty, Chrome locks onto one simple mission that takes you away from the computer. The only other way out is an annoying challenge.

Battery drains Heads-up at −5 min "Time to move." Chrome locks Mission, 5 min away "Recharged." Chrome unlocks

Product rules

V1 · each rule appears once
1 · Movement timer
Setup
Set once in the welcome flow (step 1 of 3: keep the defaults or edit). Editable later from the main screen.
Remind me every
60 min. Options: 30, 45, 60, 75, 90.
Working hours
9:00–18:00.
Days
Every day. Other option: weekdays only.
Not during lunch
12:30–13:30.
Not during meetings
Optional: connect Google Calendar. No prompt while a busy event is running.
Welcome flow also asks
Step 2: allow notifications and make them stay (set to Alerts, with a test). Step 3: add Chrome to your login items, so micro.breaks is running when you start work. Google Calendar is offered at the end.
2 · When it shows up
First unlock of the day
Inside working hours, micro.breaks opens as a tab and Chrome comes to the front. Chrome must already be running.
Every new tab
The battery and the time to the next break.
5 min before
A notification: "Nearly time to move."
Break time
A notification, and a new "Time to move." tab opens with the mission. You are switched to it automatically.
Never
Outside working hours, on days off, during lunch, during a calendar meeting. A break due in a meeting or at lunch waits until it ends.
3 · Tracking
Day start
The first keyboard or mouse activity inside working hours starts the seated timer. Chrome must be open; it can be in the background.
Seated timer
Runs while you are at the computer. Pauses under 5 min still count as seated. The battery shows what is left of the interval.
What recharges the battery
  1. A completed mission.
  2. 5+ min away from the computer without a prompt (a coffee, a locked screen).
  3. Lunch.
The seated timer then restarts from zero.
Does not recharge
A skipped break. Idle time during a calendar meeting.
Chrome was closed
Under 5 min: counted as seated. 5 min or more: one question on reopening, "Did you step away?" Yes recharges. No, or no answer, counts as seated.
4 · The break
Mission
The prompt gives you one mission. No choice of intent. Switch swaps it once per break.
Rotation
A shuffled deck of 7 missions. No repeat until all have come up.
Length
5 min. Options: 10, 15.
Start
The timer starts when you click Start mission.
Timer
It only counts down while you don't touch the keyboard or mouse. Any activity pauses it: "Step away to continue."
Lock
From the prompt until the mission is completed or skipped, Chrome pulls you back to the mission tab whenever you switch tab or window. Other apps are not blocked.
Completed
When the timer reaches zero: notification "Mission done. Welcome back.", then "Recharged." with one button, Back to work, and Chrome unlocks.
5 · Missions
Principle
So simple there is no excuse. Each one takes you away from your work.
Refill your water
Walk to the tap, fill your bottle, drink a glass there.
Climb the stairs
Two floors up and back down. No stairs nearby? Walk at a brisk pace instead.
Go for a walk
A lap of the floor, the building or the block, at your usual pace. No phone.
Daylight walk
A slow walk outside, or to an open window. Take in the natural light and some fresh air.
Tidy run
Take your cup to the kitchen, bin something, come back.
Seated stretch snack
Follow a short video on screen. One of: video 1, video 2, video 3.
Energy boost snack
Follow a short video on screen. One of: video 1, video 2.
6 · Skipping
Only way out
A quiet link, Skip (it'll cost you), on the prompt and during a mission, opens a challenge. There is no "remind me later" and no free skip.
Challenge
One of two, picked at random:
  1. Maths: 3 correct answers in a row (47 × 6, 17% of 250…). One wrong answer restarts the series.
  2. Type the sentence, exactly. Capitals and punctuation must match; pasting is blocked. One of three, never the same twice in a row:
    • "My chair and I are very happy together. Please do not disturb us."
    • "Dear future me, sorry about the neck. I had emails."
    • "Skipping this break took longer than drinking a glass of water."
Second skip of the day
5 maths answers in a row, or two different sentences.
After a skip
Chrome unlocks. The battery stays empty. The next prompt comes one interval later.

Out of scope for V1

  • Day recap, daily goal, "Today" counter, streaks and any gamification.
  • Choosing an intent (Energy, Focus, Pain relief), home / office setting.
  • Culture générale skip questions (needs a question bank).
  • Checking the mission with the camera. Blocking apps outside Chrome.
  • Accounts and sync, Outlook, mobile app, toolbar badge.

Open point

  1. Video missions. Check at build time that the 5 YouTube videos can be embedded and how long they are. Proposed: the mission lasts the video's length, 5 min at least. The design shows a fixed 5:00.

Design direction

Dark-first, one big headline, a battery that drains. Each screen has one phrase set very large ("Time to move.", "Recharged.", "Skipping costs more than moving.") and one pill to act on. The battery drains from green to amber to coral while you sit and refills when you move. Illustrations are soft 3D objects on pastel tiles; everything else stays grey.

Source of truth for the look: micro.breaks — M2 screens (mission lock). Source of truth for the rules: the PRD tab.

Principles

One big number

Each screen leads with one huge figure or phrase. Everything else is 22 px or less.

The battery is the only live color

Green, amber, coral, with a matching halo behind it. The UI chrome stays grey.

Dark by default

Dark is the default; light is one tap away and remembered. Both ship on the same tokens.

One way forward

One mission, one primary pill, Enter to start. The only exit is a quiet link that costs effort.

Celebrate the recharge

Breaks end with a short, joyful refill animation, then straight back to work.

Icons and illustration

  • UI icons: line icons, 1.75 px stroke, round caps and joins (Lucide style). 18–20 px.
  • Illustrations: Microsoft Fluent Emoji 3D (MIT). Intents: high voltage (Energy), brain (Focus), chair (Pain relief). Moves: flexed biceps, raising hands, footprints, leg, sun, ladder. Calendar for meetings. Bolt pops out of the battery on Done.
  • Video: the stage is a placeholder. V1 shows the bobbing illustration on the move's pastel tile; real exercise video comes later.

Motion

  • Battery: fill height eases linearly each second; fill "breathes" (opacity 1 → .75, 3.2 s); a light shine rises through it (3.4 s).
  • Player: illustration bobs (−22 px, ±3°, 1.6 s), paused with the timer; progress segments fill live.
  • Recharge (Done): fill 14% → 100%, coral → amber → green (2.2 s) → glow and two ripples → bolt pops and floats, eight particles burst → copy rises in, "+N min" counts up, today's dot pops.
  • Reduced motion: every animation off; final states shown directly.

Screen rules

Welcome
"WELCOME · Stay charged all day. · We help you build regular, short active breaks into your workday." Three benefits: More energy (No afternoon crash.), Sharper focus (It lasts until the work is done.), A looser body (No stiff neck or lower back.). Set it up · "Three steps, about a minute."
Setup steps
One step per screen, pastel tile on the left, "STEP 1 OF 3", progress cells "0 of 3 done".
  1. "Set your movement timer." · "Every 60 min, 9:00–18:00, every day. Not during lunch, 12:30–13:30." · Keep these · Edit
  2. "Make notifications stay." · Allow → "set Chrome to Alerts, not Banners" → Send a test → Yes, it stayed
  3. "Open Chrome at login." · "micro.breaks only runs when Chrome is open." · Done · Show me how ("System Settings › General › Login Items › + › Google Chrome")
Then "SETUP COMPLETE · All set." → Start moving · Connect Google Calendar.
Movement timer
Centred sentence: "Remind me to move every [60 min], from [9:00] to [18:00], [every day]. Not during lunch, from [12:30] to [13:30], or during [meetings]." A tray of values opens under it. "Click any highlighted word to change it."
Break prompt
Left: "Time to move.", lock chip "Chrome is locked until you move.", Start mission, Switch mission, "Skip (it'll cost you)". Right: the mission card with "YOUR MISSION", name, cue and the 5 / 10 / 15 min switch. Header hint: Enter · Start mission.
Mission
Centred: small illustration + name, cue, the ring with "TIME LEFT 3:07 of 5 min", "Leave the computer. The timer only runs while you're away.", then the skip link. Paused: "PAUSED", amber ring, "Step away to continue. You touched the keyboard or mouse."
Video mission
A 16:9 player with "Seated stretch snack · video 1 of 3" and a progress bar. Below: countdown, name, "Follow along. Hands off the keyboard.", skip link on the right.
Recharged
Refill animation → "Recharged." → Back to work. No minutes, no count. Variants add an eyebrow: "WHILE YOU WERE AWAY" or "CHROME WAS CLOSED · YOU MOVED".
Skip challenge
Left: "SKIP CHALLENGE" (second skip: "· SECOND SKIP TODAY"), "Skipping costs more than moving.", the rule line, and the primary pill ← Fine, I'll do the mission. Right: the challenge card.
  1. Maths: "Answer these questions to unlock Chrome" · "QUESTION 1 OF 3" · Check. Wrong: "Wrong. Back to zero." · Start again. Second skip: "Second skip today. 5 in a row this time."
  2. Sentence: "Type it exactly. No pasting." · "Capitals and punctuation count." · on a mistake, "One wrong character. Fix it to continue." Second skip: "Two sentences this time.", "SENTENCE 2 OF 2".
  3. Passed: "CHALLENGE PASSED · CHROME IS UNLOCKED · Skipped. · Your battery stays empty. Next break at 12:04." → Back to work.
New tab
Wordmark and theme toggle only. Battery with halo → "NEXT BREAK IN" + countdown → "42 min since your last active break" → Start a break now + chip "Every 60 min · 9:00–18:00".
New tab states
  1. After a skip: empty still battery, "BREAK SKIPPED · NEXT BREAK IN 52:10", "1 h 08 since your last active break".
  2. Before hours: grey battery, "BEFORE WORKING HOURS · 9:00 · Your day starts at 9:00, at your first activity."
  3. Lunch: battery refilling, "LUNCH · 12:30–13:30 · Lunch. · Tracking paused until 13:30. Your battery will be full."
  4. Meeting: pill "In a meeting until 11:30. Prompts wait."
  5. Prompt held: "BREAK DUE AT 11:05 · In a meeting. · Your break is waiting. It opens at 11:30, when the meeting ends."
  6. Done for today: "FRIDAY · 18:00 · Done for today. · See you tomorrow."
  7. Weekend: "SATURDAY · Weekend. · See you Monday at 9:00."
  8. Chrome was closed: "CHROME WAS CLOSED FOR 40 MIN · Did you step away? · Your battery depends on it." Yes, I moved · No, I kept working. "No answer counts as seated."
  9. Health line: "Notifications are off. micro.breaks can't reach you outside Chrome." Turn on.
Notifications
  1. −5 min "Nearly time to move." · "Get ready for your active break in 5 min." · Start break now
  2. 0 min "Time to move." · "1 h 00 seated. Your break is ready in Chrome." · Start break
  3. Timer ends "Mission done. Welcome back." · "+6 min of movement. Battery recharged." · Open

Voice

  • Short, calm, second person. Headlines are a few words and a full stop: "Time to move.", "Recharged.", "Skipped."
  • Actions say what happens: "Start mission", "Switch mission", "Back to work", "Fine, I'll do the mission".
  • Dry humour only where the user is avoiding the break: "Skip (it'll cost you)", "Skipping costs more than moving.", "Wrong. Back to zero."
  • Mission cues are one physical instruction: "Walk to the tap, fill your bottle, drink a glass there."

Accessibility

  • Countdowns use role="timer"; the battery is role="img" with a text label. The paused state is announced ("…seconds left, paused").
  • Enter starts the mission. Every control has a visible focus state. The length switch uses aria-pressed.
  • The skip challenge works with the keyboard alone; errors are stated in text, not by color only.
  • prefers-reduced-motion turns off breathing, shine, floating illustrations and the recharge sequence.

Status: not started. Cost ~€0 through the test week.

Architecture

One rules engine holds every product rule from the PRD as a pure function: step(state, input, now) → { state, effects }. Inputs are ticks, idle changes and user actions. Effects are "show nudge", "open prompt", "log event". The background service worker feeds it and executes the effects. Every screen reads state and sends actions; no screen contains rule logic.

MV3 service workers sleep, so state is saved to storage after every step and restored on wake.

src/
  engine/        rules engine (pure) + tests      ← the PRD in code
  background/    service worker: idle, alarms, notifications, windows
  entrypoints/   newtab/ setup/ settings/ mission/ skip/ done/
  ui/            design-system components (pill, flow card, stepper…)
  data/          Dexie db, event log, derived day stats
content/missions.json
docs/spec.html   this document, the source of truth
docs/design/     Claude Design export (screens)

Trade-offs

Extension now, web app later

Only an extension runs without an open tab, opens itself when Chrome starts, owns the new tab and can switch you to a tab when a break is due. Sharing and accounts come with a web app in M2.

Laptop activity as a proxy for sitting

Cheap and automatic, but a standing desk or a call without typing fools it. Calendar holds cover the worst case (a silent call).

60-min rhythm, not 30

The evidence favours moving every 30 min. 60 min is the ceiling a busy workday will accept; tighten it once the habit holds.

Local only, event log first

No account friction for the test week. The log shape is the sync contract, so M2 adds a backend without reworking data.

Lock inside Chrome only

An extension can pull you back to the mission tab, not block Slack or VS Code. It still sees you typing, so the mission timer does not move. A native app would be needed for a full lock.

"Away from the keyboard" as proof

Wayk checks missions with the phone camera. Here the only cheap proof is no keyboard or mouse input while the timer runs. You could sit still for 5 min; accepted for V1.

Chrome must be running

An extension can't launch Chrome. The welcome screen asks you to add Chrome to your login items; without it, nothing happens until you open Chrome.

Calendar in M1, Google only

The design replaced "Can't move now" with calendar-aware prompts. Google via chrome.identity is a few hours of work; Outlook needs its own OAuth flow and waits for M2.
